sections.name: Owlbear
sections.card:
Summary: A cross between a bear and an owl that hugs like a bear and attacks with its beak; Baldur's Gate 3 lists owlbears among its Forgotten Realms monsters.
Tips: In the tabletop lore an owlbear is a meat-eater with a fierce temper. A mated pair shares a cave, and it will go after anything larger than a mouse.

sections.name: Githyanki Warriors
sections.card:
Summary: A race of warriors, almost always evil, who attack the mind flayer ship at the start of the game riding red dragons.
Tips: They are after a companion's prism. Tabletop lore calls them ancient enemies of the githzerai, and says they began as the slave army that rose against the mind flayers.

sections.name: Minthara
sections.card:
Summary: A drow paladin who leads a band of goblins and other creatures for the game's antagonist in the first act and clashes with the Emerald Grove refugee settlement.
Tips: You can join her raid on the grove, fight her and kill her along with her goblins, or skip the raid and spare her: either knock her out with non-lethal damage while you kill her commanders, or simply leave her alone.
Tips: If you skip the raid and spare her, the grove is lost.

sections.name: Goblin Horde
sections.card:
Summary: Goblins are evil humanoids, a common and weaker monster kind in the tabletop game. In the first act a goblin horde that worships a cult of the Absolute is up against the druids and the tiefling refugees at the Emerald Grove.
Tips: The first-edition tabletop monster book describes goblins as a tribal society in dismal surroundings, and low-level characters often face them. The first act's locations include a goblin camp, and Minthara leads a band of goblins in that act.

sections.name: Explosive Barrel
sections.card:
Summary: A barrel that counts as an item you can store in your camp stash and as an environmental element you can exploit in combat.
Uses: In a fight, explosive barrels are part of the surroundings you can turn to your advantage.
Tips: You can send a barrel to your camp stash and take it out again later.

sections.name: Potions
sections.card:
Summary: Drinkable items, including health potions and one that lets you talk to animals.
Uses: Drinking a potion consumes a bonus action; attacking with a sword or casting a spell consumes an action.
Tips: Actions, bonus actions and movement are separate turn resources, so a potion does not cost you your attack or spell.

sections.name: Weapon Poison
sections.card:
Summary: Poison that weapons can be dipped in, one of the combat options the game lists beside exploiting explosive barrels.
Tips: You apply it by using the poison item itself, much as you would use a health potion. Polygon's reviewer thought that was unintuitive.
